cards.title: Bharata / The Empty Throne
cards.mythicAnchor: Bharata refuses the kingship obtained through Kaikeyi’s demands; seeks Rama’s return; accepts stewardship under Rama’s sovereignty.
cards.core: RIGHTFUL PLACE — To recognize the responsibility that is truly yours—and to refuse what is not yours, even when it is available, prestigious, expected, or advantageous.
cards.prakasha: STEWARDSHIP — You know what belongs to you and what does not. You can carry responsibility without needing to possess everything entrusted to you. Recognition, power, inheritance or opportunity do not override inner and ethical clarity.
cards.chhaya: THE BORROWED THRONE — Living inside a role that is not truly yours because it was offered, inherited, expected, admired or convenient. The distortion is confusing capability, expectation or opportunity with rightful responsibility.
cards.marga: DISCERN BEFORE YOU ACCEPT — Do not ask only what you are capable of carrying. Ask what is actually yours to carry.

cards.title: Arjuna / The Lowered Bow
cards.mythicAnchor: Arjuna lowers his bow before battle; Krishna explicitly invokes his svadharma as a kshatriya in the Bhagavad Gita.
cards.core: THE NECESSARY ACT — What remains yours to do even when emotion makes withdrawal feel cleaner.
cards.prakasha: COURAGE TO ENGAGE — Acting without waiting for comfort, certainty or desire.
cards.chhaya: NOBLE AVOIDANCE — Using sensitivity, doubt or moral language to escape a responsibility that still remains yours.
cards.marga: NAME THE DUTY — Separate your feelings about the task from whether the task is yours.

cards.title: Dharmavyadha / The Butcher's Stall
cards.mythicAnchor: In the Mahabharata Vana Parva, the righteous meat-seller teaches Kaushika about dharma through ordinary work and devoted service to his parents.
cards.core: THE DUTY BEFORE YOU — Sacredness may lie in faithfully doing the work actually entrusted to your life, not escaping into a more impressive identity.
cards.prakasha: DIGNITY OF SERVICE — Presence, competence and care in ordinary responsibility.
cards.chhaya: BORROWED HOLINESS — Abandoning real obligations for a role that looks spiritually or socially superior.
cards.marga: HONOR THE NEAR DUTY — Attend first to the responsibility already standing before you.

cards.title: Kacha / The Knowledge Entrusted
cards.mythicAnchor: The devas entrust Kacha with obtaining Shukra's Sanjivani knowledge; he accepts discipleship and repeatedly suffers death while pursuing the mission.
cards.core: THE ENTRUSTED TASK — Some duties become yours because they have been consciously entrusted to you and you have accepted the charge.
cards.prakasha: FIDELITY TO MISSION — Remembering what you came to do despite distraction, hardship or changing circumstances.
cards.chhaya: MISSION POSSESSION — Allowing an assigned task to consume identity, relationships or judgment simply because you once agreed to it.
cards.marga: RETURN TO THE CHARGE — Name what was actually entrusted to you. Separate the mission from everything you have added to it.

cards.title: Bhagiratha / The Ancestral River
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagiratha undertakes severe effort to bring Ganga to earth so Sagara's descendants may receive liberation, completing work earlier generations could not.
cards.core: THE UNFINISHED INHERITANCE — Some responsibilities arrive before you do; your task is to decide which inherited work genuinely asks completion through you.
cards.prakasha: ANCESTRAL RESPONSIBILITY — Completing worthy work without needing to have originated it.
cards.chhaya: INHERITED BURDEN — Carrying family or lineage obligations simply because previous generations left them unresolved.
cards.marga: TEST THE INHERITANCE — Continue what is worthy; do not confuse ancestry with automatic obligation.

cards.title: Garuda / The Price of Freedom
cards.mythicAnchor: Garuda learns of Vinata's enslavement, asks what act can free her, and undertakes the demand to obtain amrita.
cards.core: THE LIBERATING RESPONSIBILITY — A responsibility may become yours when you truly see a bondage affecting someone bound to your life and possess the agency to answer it.
cards.prakasha: RESPONSIVE STRENGTH — Using power to release rather than dominate; turning capacity toward liberation.
cards.chhaya: RESCUER'S BONDAGE — Making another person's captivity the whole of your identity, or assuming every suffering person is yours to save.
cards.marga: ASK WHAT FREEDOM REQUIRES — Identify the actual bondage, your relationship to it, and the action that can genuinely change it.

cards.title: Vidura / The Counsel Unheard
cards.mythicAnchor: Vidura states that true beneficial counsel should be spoken even unasked and repeatedly counsels Dhritarashtra during the Kuru crisis.
cards.core: THE DUTY WITHOUT CONTROL — Your responsibility may be to speak, warn, advise or serve rightly even when the outcome is not yours to command.
cards.prakasha: FAITHFUL COUNSEL — Doing the work of your role clearly and truthfully without confusing influence with control.
cards.chhaya: FUTILE CONTROL — Believing that being right entitles you to make another person obey.
cards.marga: FULFIL YOUR PART — Say what must be said, do what belongs to your role, and release the outcome that belongs to another.

cards.title: Janaka / The Work That Remains
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagavad Gita 3.20 invokes Janaka and others as attaining perfection through action and urges action with lokasangraha in view.
cards.core: RESPONSIBILITY AFTER ATTAINMENT — Inner freedom does not automatically cancel the work your position still requires from you.
cards.prakasha: ENGAGED FREEDOM — Acting without personal hunger for the reward because the work still serves the whole.
cards.chhaya: SPIRITUAL WITHDRAWAL — Using detachment, success or self-sufficiency as permission to abandon necessary participation.
cards.marga: STAY WHERE YOU STILL SERVE — Freedom from needing the role is not always freedom from performing it.

cards.title: Hanuman / The Leap Only You Can Make
cards.mythicAnchor: At the despondent search party, Jambavan identifies Hanuman's exceptional capacity to cross the ocean; Hanuman rises and prepares for the leap.
cards.core: THE CAPACITY THAT CALLS — Sometimes a responsibility becomes yours because the situation requires what you, specifically, are able to give.
cards.prakasha: CAPABILITY IN SERVICE — Recognizing your real strength and placing it at the service of a need larger than self-display.
cards.chhaya: SAVIOR IDENTITY — Assuming that because you can do something, you must do everything; turning exceptional capacity into permanent obligation.
cards.marga: MAKE YOUR LEAP — Identify the task for which your particular capacity is actually needed. Give that capacity fully there—not everywhere.

cards.title: Shibi / The Scale
cards.mythicAnchor: In the Mahabharata hawk-and-pigeon episode, King Shibi protects the refuge-seeking pigeon and ultimately places himself on the scale when flesh cannot balance its weight.
cards.core: COMPASSION WITH WEIGHT — Virtue becomes real when protection costs the protector something.
cards.prakasha: COSTLY COMPASSION — Protecting the vulnerable with personal stake rather than sentiment alone.
cards.chhaya: MARTYRDOM — Proving goodness through needless self-destruction or making sacrifice itself the virtue.
cards.marga: MEASURE THE SACRIFICE — Protect what needs protection without worshipping your own suffering.

cards.title: Jatayu / The Broken Wing
cards.mythicAnchor: In Valmiki Ramayana Aranya Kanda 50–51, the aged Jaṭāyu confronts Rāvaṇa during Sītā's abduction and fights despite the unequal contest.
cards.core: COURAGE THAT INTERVENES — Virtue is not merely knowing what is wrong; sometimes goodness must enter the danger it recognizes.
cards.prakasha: MORAL COURAGE — Acting to protect another even when success is uncertain and the cost may be personal.
cards.chhaya: HEROIC IMPULSE — Throwing yourself into every conflict to prove courage, without judging whether intervention helps.
cards.marga: ENTER THE NECESSARY DANGER — When protection truly requires your presence, do not let poor odds become an excuse for absence.

cards.title: Yudhishthira / The Faithful Dog
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahaprasthanika Parva, Yudhiṣṭhira refuses Indra's heavenly chariot if admission requires abandoning the dog that faithfully followed him; the dog reveals itself as Dharma.
cards.core: LOYALTY AT THE THRESHOLD — Character is revealed by whom you refuse to discard when advancement makes loyalty inconvenient.
cards.prakasha: FAITHFULNESS — Remaining responsible to a dependent or companion even when abandonment would benefit you.
cards.chhaya: BLIND LOYALTY — Preserving attachment after care has become complicity, harm or refusal to let go.
cards.marga: NOTICE WHO PAYS FOR YOUR ASCENT — Before taking the next step, ask whether your gain requires betraying someone who trusted you.

cards.title: Savitri / The Road Beyond Death
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Vana Parva, after Satyavān dies, Sāvitrī follows Yama, converses with him through successive boons, and persists until Satyavān's life is restored.
cards.core: STEADFAST LOVE — Love becomes virtue when devotion can remain intelligent, articulate and purposeful in the presence of loss.
cards.prakasha: DEVOTED PRESENCE — Staying with what you love through fear and grief without surrendering clarity or agency.
cards.chhaya: REFUSAL OF REALITY — Calling attachment 'devotion' when it cannot accept endings, limits, autonomy or change.
cards.marga: FOLLOW WITH OPEN EYES — Stay faithful without becoming blind; let love sharpen your intelligence rather than replace it.

cards.title: Rantideva / The Last Cup
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagavata Purana 9.21 describes Rantideva, after prolonged hunger and thirst, repeatedly sharing received food and finally his remaining water with a thirsty outcaste guest.
cards.core: GENEROSITY WITHOUT SURPLUS — Giving reveals its depth when generosity is not merely the distribution of what you will not miss.
cards.prakasha: OPEN-HANDEDNESS — Sharing resources, dignity and care without reducing generosity to leftovers.
cards.chhaya: SELF-ERASURE — Giving until deprivation becomes identity, performance or neglect of legitimate responsibilities to self and dependents.
cards.marga: GIVE WHAT MATTERS, NOT YOUR EXISTENCE — Let generosity cost something without making your destruction its proof.

cards.title: Yudhishthira / The Two Mothers
cards.mythicAnchor: In the Yaksha episode of Mahabharata Vana Parva, offered the life of one brother, Yudhiṣṭhira chooses Nakula so that both Kuntī and Mādrī will each retain a living son.
cards.core: IMPARTIAL CARE — Virtue sometimes asks you to distribute concern by principle rather than preference.
cards.prakasha: FAIRNESS — Giving legitimate claims weight even when affection, usefulness or self-interest pulls elsewhere.
cards.chhaya: FALSE EQUALITY — Treating unequal needs as identical merely to appear impartial, or using fairness to avoid compassionate judgment.
cards.marga: COUNT THE ABSENT CLAIM — Ask whose interest disappears when you choose only by closeness, utility or preference.

cards.title: Prahlada / The Unshaken Heart
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagavata Purana 7.5 presents Prahlāda openly teaching devotion to Viṣṇu despite his father Hiraṇyakaśipu's hostility; later chapters narrate the persecution arising from that devotion.
cards.core: INNER CONSTANCY — Virtue can mean remaining inwardly aligned when authority, fear or belonging pressures you to betray what you hold sacred.
cards.prakasha: DEVOTIONAL INTEGRITY — Keeping faith with a deeply held good without needing external permission.
cards.chhaya: RIGID CERTAINTY — Mistaking stubbornness, sectarian superiority or refusal to listen for principled conviction.
cards.marga: STAND WITHOUT HARDENING — Protect the center you cannot betray while keeping the heart from becoming another fortress.

cards.title: Damayanti / The Chosen One
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Vana Parva, Damayantī chooses Nala at her svayaṃvara even when gods appear in Nala's likeness, and the narrative later tests their bond through separation and hardship.
cards.core: FIDELITY TO RECOGNITION — Virtue is the capacity to remain true to a choice you made with clear recognition when glamour, status or difficulty tries to rewrite it.
cards.prakasha: CONSTANCY — Honoring a freely made commitment through changing circumstances without confusing hardship with invalidity.
cards.chhaya: LOYALTY TO THE PAST — Staying because you once chose, even after truth, safety or the relationship itself has fundamentally changed.
cards.marga: RECOGNIZE AGAIN — Do not obey an old promise mechanically; ask whether the truth you chose is still present now.

cards.title: Ambarisha / The Sip of Water
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagavata Purana 9.4.39–41 presents Ambarīṣa balancing the deadline of his Dvādaśī vow against hospitality owed to the absent Durvāsā, choosing only water and then waiting for the guest.
cards.core: RESTRAINT BETWEEN CLAIMS — Good character is often the disciplined search for the least harmful action when two legitimate obligations collide.
cards.prakasha: MEASURED RESTRAINT — Refusing the dramatic extreme and choosing an action that preserves as much of both duties as possible.
cards.chhaya: VIRTUE BY TECHNICALITY — Hiding behind clever compromise, ritual correctness or minimal compliance to avoid the moral substance of a conflict.
cards.marga: FIND THE NARROW PATH — When two duties compete, seek the smallest action that violates neither more than necessary.

cards.title: Bhishma / The Terrible Vow
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Adi Parva, Devavrata renounces succession and vows lifelong brahmacarya so Satyavati's descendants can inherit.
cards.core: VOW AS ARCHITECTURE — A boundary you freely choose can organize an entire life; judge a vow by the future it will govern.
cards.prakasha: COMMITTED LIMIT — Giving up a real option consciously so action gains coherence, trust and direction.
cards.chhaya: THE PRISON OF YOUR OWN WORD — Preserving an old vow after its purpose changes because identity depends on it.
cards.marga: VOW WITH FORESIGHT — Ask what the promise protects, excludes and who else will live inside its consequences.

cards.title: Rama / The Fourteen Years
cards.mythicAnchor: In Valmiki Ramayana Ayodhya Kanda, Rama accepts fourteen years of exile in relation to Dasharatha's boons and word.
cards.core: THE WORD YOU INHERIT — Sometimes you become bearer of a promise you did not make; test whether honoring it preserves rightful order.
cards.prakasha: FIDELITY TO TRUST — Carrying a legitimate commitment whose credibility now depends upon your conduct.
cards.chhaya: INHERITED CAPTIVITY — Treating every promise made by family or predecessor as automatically binding upon you.
cards.marga: TEST THE BORROWED WORD — Ask whose promise this is, what good it protects and whether you truly have standing to carry it.

cards.title: Karna / The Four Spared
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Karna refuses Kunti's requested realignment but pledges to spare four Pandava brothers, leaving Arjuna as his opponent.
cards.core: THE BOUNDED PROMISE — Even inside conflict, a chosen limit can prevent total escalation.
cards.prakasha: RESTRAINT WITHIN CONFLICT — Drawing a line that preserves some humanity without pretending the conflict disappeared.
cards.chhaya: SELECTIVE MORALITY — Using one noble restriction to excuse the rest of a destructive course.
cards.marga: NAME WHAT REMAINS FORBIDDEN — When you cannot leave the conflict, define the acts you still refuse to commit.

cards.title: Ekalavya / The Severed Thumb
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Adi Parva, Ekalavya gives his right thumb when Drona demands it as guru-dakshina.
cards.core: WHEN REVERENCE CROSSES THE SELF — Respect for authority becomes distortion when obedience surrenders what authority has no rightful claim to demand.
cards.prakasha: DIGNIFIED BOUNDARY — Honoring teachers and traditions without abandoning the right to evaluate what they ask.
cards.chhaya: SANCTIFIED SELF-ERASURE — Calling an unequal or destructive demand sacred merely because it comes from authority.
cards.marga: RESPECT DOES NOT CANCEL DISCERNMENT — Ask whether the demand is legitimate, proportionate and truly owed.

cards.title: Gandhari / The Folded Cloth
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Adi Parva, Gandhari learns Dhritarashtra is blind and binds her own eyes with folded cloth before marriage.
cards.core: THE LIMIT YOU CHOOSE TO SHARE — Solidarity can involve voluntary limitation, but shared suffering is not automatically shared understanding.
cards.prakasha: SOLIDARITY — Willingly accepting a meaningful constraint so another is not left alone inside theirs.
cards.chhaya: IMITATED WOUND — Reproducing another's deprivation until empathy becomes self-disablement or performance.
cards.marga: SHARE THE BURDEN, NOT NECESSARILY THE WOUND — Ask whether your chosen limitation actually helps the person you mean to honor.

cards.title: Bali / The Three Paces
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagavata Purana 8.19–20 presents Vamana's three-pace request, Shukra's warning, and Bali's decision to honor his promise despite the revealed consequence.
cards.core: THE PROMISE AFTER THE WARNING — A promise reveals its weight when new information makes keeping it costly.
cards.prakasha: ACCOUNTABILITY TO YOUR WORD — Refusing to treat inconvenience alone as sufficient reason to abandon commitment.
cards.chhaya: PRIDE IN CONSISTENCY — Keeping a promise because retreat would wound self-image even when reconsideration may be responsible.
cards.marga: REASSESS WITHOUT SELF-DECEPTION — New information deserves review; neither convenience nor pride should decide.

cards.title: Yudhishthira / The Half-Truth
cards.mythicAnchor: In Mahabharata Drona Parva, Yudhishthira says Ashvatthaman is dead and adds 'the elephant' indistinctly, inducing Drona to believe his son has died.
cards.core: THE EDGE OF TRUTH — Principles can collide with catastrophe; danger lies in manipulating the letter of virtue while claiming its authority.
cards.prakasha: MORAL SERIOUSNESS — Recognizing exceptions to a principle carry residue and cannot be made casually clean by clever wording.
cards.chhaya: TECHNICAL TRUTH — Saying something literally defensible while deliberately engineering a false belief.
cards.marga: OWN THE EXCEPTION — If necessity crosses a principle, name the breach and its cost instead of laundering it into innocence.

cards.title: Lakshmana / The Hut Left Behind
cards.mythicAnchor: In Valmiki Ramayana Aranya Kanda 45, Lakshmana initially remains with Sita under Rama's entrusted instruction, then leaves after severe accusations.
cards.core: THE BOUNDARY UNDER PRESSURE — A limit is hardest to keep when fear and accusation make maintaining it look cruel or disloyal.
cards.prakasha: STEADY GUARDIANSHIP — Holding a necessary boundary through emotional intensity while continuing to listen and explain.
cards.chhaya: COERCED ABANDONMENT — Letting accusation, guilt or panic force you out of a responsibility you still believe necessary.
cards.marga: DO NOT LET SHAME DECIDE — Reassess the boundary on evidence and duty, not merely on the pain of being misunderstood.

cards.title: The Rules Before War
cards.mythicAnchor: Mahabharata Bhishma Parva opens with the opposing sides agreeing rules governing fair combat and protected persons before battle.
cards.core: LIMITS EVEN IN CONFLICT — Maryada is most visible when power agrees beforehand that some acts remain unacceptable even against an enemy.
cards.prakasha: RECIPROCAL RESTRAINT — Establishing rules that protect dignity, proportionality and the vulnerable before passions peak.
cards.chhaya: RULES FOR APPEARANCE — Celebrating codes that are ignored when obedience becomes inconvenient or using formal rules to disguise brutality.
cards.marga: SET THE LINE BEFORE THE HEAT — Define limits before conflict tests them, and judge integrity by whether they survive advantage.

cards.title: Ajamila / The Life of Drift
cards.chhaya: Calling gradual decline harmless because no single step feels decisive
cards.marga: NOTICE THE DIRECTION, NOT ONLY THE STEP

cards.title: Rama / The Empty Ayodhya
cards.core: THE PLACE THAT REMAINS AFTER THE PERSON
cards.marga: LET MEMORY INHABIT, NOT OCCUPY, THE WHOLE KINGDOM

cards.title: Sita / The Earth Receives Her
cards.prakasha: Allowing dignity to close what cannot be repaired
cards.chhaya: Demanding one more proof from the departed
cards.marga: LET THE END BE AN END

cards.title: Nanda / The Chariot to Mathura
cards.core: THE CHILD WHO DOES NOT RETURN WITH YOU
cards.marga: BLESS THE ROAD THAT TAKES THEM BEYOND YOU

cards.title: Gopis / The Message from Mathura
cards.prakasha: Letting longing deepen meaning without denying distance
cards.chhaya: Living only in the imagined return
cards.marga: LET LONGING SPEAK WITHOUT MAKING IT A PRISON

cards.title: Kunti / The Son Not Named
cards.prakasha: Naming what secrecy cost after truth emerges
cards.marga: MOURN WHAT CANNOT NOW BE GIVEN

cards.title: Gandhari / The Hundred Fires Gone
cards.prakasha: Making room for grief too large to solve
cards.chhaya: Turning bereavement into permanent curse against life
cards.marga: DO NOT ASK GRIEF TO BECOME SMALL BEFORE YOU CARRY IT

cards.title: Urmila / The Fourteen-Year Absence
cards.mythicAnchor: Ramayana tradition: Urmila remains in Ayodhya during Lakshmana's exile; details vary across later traditions.
cards.prakasha: Continuing one's own life while someone beloved is away
cards.chhaya: Erasing the one who remained because the absent story seems grander
cards.marga: HONOR THE LIFE THAT WAITED

cards.title: Damayanti / The Empty Forest
cards.chhaya: Making another's disappearance proof of your worthlessness
cards.marga: SEEK THEM WITHOUT LOSING YOURSELF

cards.title: Uddhava / The Departure
cards.mythicAnchor: Bhagavata Purana 11, Uddhava Gita and Krishna's departure context
cards.core: THE TEACHING LEFT AFTER THE TEACHER
cards.marga: BECOME A CARRIER OF WHAT THE ABSENCE TAUGHT

cards.title: Radha / The Absent Flute
cards.mythicAnchor: LATER DEVOTIONAL TRADITIONS: Radha-centered viraha becomes central in works such as Jayadeva's Gita Govinda and later Vaishnava devotional literature; Radha is not named as Krishna's principal beloved in the Bhagavata Purana text itself.
cards.core: LONGING THAT MAKES ABSENCE PRESENT — Viraha is separation, grief, longing and the altered world created by absence.
cards.prakasha: DEVOTIONAL LONGING — Allowing love and grief to coexist with continuing life.
cards.chhaya: ROMANTICIZATION OF DEPRIVATION — Making absence the only remaining identity or proof of love.
cards.marga: LET LONGING REVEAL VALUE WITHOUT MAKING PAIN THE PROOF OF LOVE — Give the absence a form that can be carried.
